To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students learn 21 st century skills when teachers teach them in ways that are relevant to their lives and that are consistent with what we know about how students learn.
1) students learn best when they learn 21st Century skills and 2) they learn 21 Century skills best when they are explicitly taught.
Students are not developing 21st century skill because they are not explicitly taught them, because they are not assessed as well, and because the outdated, transmission model is still dominant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
making curriculum relevant to students' learning, but we also need to make learning itself more relevant to students' daily lives.
how to make curriculum relevant, not just relevant.
the big picture of learning, with how to make learning whole, with how to teach the whole game.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students need to see how the content they learn fits into a larger context, and they need to see the relevance of what they are learning to their own lives.
, to be effective, curriculum should be relevant to students.
the relevance of a specific curriculum is clearer to students if they understand how it is connected to other topics, and to the big picture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students must know how the content of their learning fits into the bigger picture.
we need to make the learning whole for the students.
students need to know how the topic at hand fits into the bigger picture and how the topic is relevant to their lives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
relevance is not about what students think is interesting, but what they need to know to make sense of the world.
students are more motivated to learn if they understand why it matters.
